headline: Highest risk is medium: Perplexity can ingest uploaded documents and web context, but LightZero has no filesystem, network, or MCP surfaces to feed or act on them.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A plausible injection path exists only if LightZero outputs are manually copied into Perplexity or uploaded as files; LightZero has no I/O surfaces, while Perplexity parses uploaded documents and browsing context. That makes hijack possible but not default, and the blast radius is limited to the copied artifact.
conditions: IF LightZero outputs are manually pasted into Perplexity prompts or uploaded documents
IF Perplexity is asked to follow instructions embedded in those artifacts
mitigations: Avoid pasting model outputs into Perplexity without stripping instructions
Use a fixed prompt template that ignores embedded directives
Upload only sanitized excerpts, not raw agent transcripts
Mark copied content as untrusted in the operator workflow

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightZero touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network egress, while Perplexity handles uploaded documents and browsing context. Leakage requires the operator to place sensitive material into Perplexity; there is no evidence of an automatic shared workspace or host-level bridge between the pair.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are uploaded into Perplexity
IF LightZero outputs are copied into Perplexity alongside sensitive context
mitigations: Do not upload sensitive files to Perplexity
Redact secrets before any copy-paste into Perplexity
Keep LightZero and Perplexity in separate workspaces
Review Perplexity sharing settings before use

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No write-conflict pathway is visible: LightZero cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, and Perplexity is vendor-hosted with no host execution and no filesystem write surface. Without overlapping mutable resources, concurrent corruption is not plausible.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or git repo
IF an external orchestrator introduces shared mutable state
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in the same workflow
Do not mount a shared writable directory
Avoid giving either agent git credentials
Use separate user accounts or containers

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity can treat copied LightZero outputs as authoritative if the operator feeds them in, and Perplexity’s citation-rich answers may then be reused downstream. LightZero itself does not act on outputs, so the cascade is one-way and depends on manual transfer, but the default risk is still meaningful because verification is not guaranteed.
conditions: IF LightZero-generated text is used as source material for Perplexity answers
IF the operator forwards Perplexity answers into downstream decisions without independent verification
mitigations: Require a human check before reusing Perplexity outputs
Ask Perplexity to cite primary sources, not LightZero text
Separate generation and verification steps
Flag LightZero outputs as untrusted drafts

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is evident from LightZero, while Perplexity documents handling and vendor-hosted processing are documented. Because only Perplexity has meaningful data handling surfaces, compliance risk is limited to operator-chosen uploads rather than an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into Perplexity
IF the operator requires a residency or retention guarantee not provided by Perplexity
mitigations: Do not send regulated data to Perplexity
Check the privacy policy before uploading documents
Use anonymized or synthetic inputs
Keep compliance-sensitive workflows offline
